title: macOS: headset power on/off emits spurious play/pause → phantom record toggle
description:
## Summary
On the macOS app, powering the BlueParrott headset OFF or ON spuriously toggles the mic record state. A power transition is misread as a button press.

## Root cause
HeadsetRemoteCommandManager (macOS) holds the Now Playing slot (continuous silent audio, reported `.playing`) and registers MPRemoteCommandCenter play/pause/toggle handlers. When the headset disconnects (power off) macOS sends a `pause` transport command; when it connects (power on) a `play`. `handlePause()` treats ❚❚ as a toggle (intentional for AirPods single-press), and `handlePlay()` starts recording from `.ready` — so each power transition fires `startRecording()`.

This is the unreliable-proxy class of behavior the macOS-BlueParrott-CoreBluetooth epic exists to replace; it is NOT caused by the Phase A2 GATT explorer (which only logs).

## Evidence (logs-20260602-213403.txt)
21:32:36.997 [HeadsetRemote] Headset: ❚❚ received — state=Ready
21:32:37.003 [HeadsetRemote] Headset: recording started
21:32:37.242 [BPExplore]    disconnected: ...device has disconnected from us.
(pause command arrives ~245ms before the BLE disconnect = the power-off.)
No [BluetoothAudio] lines → the CoreAudio mute-proxy/PTT is OFF and is not involved.

## Repro
macOS app, headset control enabled, BlueParrott connected. Toggle the headset power off, then on. Observe record start/stop with no button press.

## Fix options
1. Targeted mitigation: ignore play/pause/toggle MPRemoteCommandCenter commands that arrive within ~1.5s of a BlueParrott BLE connect/disconnect (keeps AirPods PTT working). Add unit tests.
2. Superseded by voice-code-macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth-b4i.6 (rewire macOS to drive BlueParrottBLEManager GATT button events and retire the media-key/mute proxies as the BlueParrott trigger).

## Caveat
A naive 'don't start recording on pause' breaks AirPods PTT, which relies on the ❚❚-as-toggle behavior. Any fix must preserve that.

## Acceptance
Powering the BlueParrott headset off/on does NOT change record state on macOS; AirPods single-press PTT still works.

title: macOS BlueParrott button via CoreBluetooth
description:
## Design Document
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md

## Overview
Detect BlueParrott multifunction-button events on macOS by reimplementing the
iOS BPHeadset SDK's BLE GATT integration directly on CoreBluetooth, since the
SDK xcframework ships iOS-only slices. Replaces the current (broken) CoreAudio
mute-proxy trigger that never sees the button.

- Phase A: a DEBUG-only collector that captures the proprietary GATT protocol
  (characteristic UUIDs, App-Mode enable handshake, button-event byte format) by
  instrumenting the working iOS SDK, plus an App-Mode persistence experiment
  that decides Phase B's scope.
- Phase B: a macOS CoreBluetooth client + pure byte parser feeding the existing
  BlueParrottButtonDelegate / HeadsetRemoteCommandManager state machine unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. macOS button down starts recording and up stops+sends, matching iOS PTT behavior.
2. macOS tap / double-tap / long-press map to the same actions as iOS
   (HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.swift:626-665).
3. BlueParrottEventParser unit tests pass against the captured real-device byte
   sequences for all five gestures, and return nil for empty/unknown payloads.
4. Connect/retry/re-arm unit tests pass with a faked BLECentral (no hardware).
5. Out-of-range disconnect returns the state machine to ready and reconnects
   automatically when the headset returns.
6. make build-mac (scheme VoiceCodeMac) succeeds with
   com.apple.security.device.bluetooth added; make build (iOS) is unchanged.
7. The Phase A collector (BPSniffer) is absent from release builds
   (#if DEBUG verified by a release-config build).
8. make test-mac passes (runs the new macOS VoiceCodeMacTests) and make test
   still passes (iOS suite, no regression).

title: Build Phase A1 DEBUG GATT collector (BPSniffer) to capture the BlueParrott protocol
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase A1 — passive observer)

## Context
Unblocking step. The proprietary GATT protocol (characteristic UUIDs, App-Mode enable handshake, per-gesture byte format) is not in the public SDK header — capture it by instrumenting the working iOS BPHeadset SDK.

## Requirements
- [ ] New `BPSniffer.swift`, gated `#if DEBUG && os(iOS)`
- [ ] Swizzle `CBPeripheral.writeValue(_:for:type:)` → log characteristic UUID + payload hex
- [ ] Discover the SDK's peripheral delegate at runtime and swizzle `peripheral:didUpdateValueForCharacteristic:` → log UUID + value hex
- [ ] Route all output through `LogManager.shared.log(category: "BPSniff")`
- [ ] Install the hook from a DEBUG entry point when BlueParrott is enabled
- [ ] On hardware: capture the App-Mode enable write (char + bytes) and each gesture's notification (char + bytes) for down/up/tap/double-tap/long-press

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's Code Examples (BPSniffer). Objective-C runtime method swizzling.
- New files: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BPSniffer.swift`
- Dependencies: none (iOS already has the BLE entitlement and links the working SDK)

## Verification
- [ ] Manual (hardware): iOS DEBUG build, enable BlueParrott, press all 5 gestures → "BPSniff" logs show the enable-write and per-gesture bytes
- [ ] Release-config build confirms `BPSniffer` is compiled out

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #7 (collector absent from release builds); produces the captured bytes that epic #3 depends on.

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: "Add macOS Bluetooth entitlement and usage description".

title: Wire BlueParrott button events: subscribe, parse, dispatch, conditional App-Mode enable
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase B happy path + byte parser)

## Context
Completes the macOS client on top of the core/lifecycle task: subscribe to the button-event characteristic, parse via `BlueParrottEventParser`, dispatch to the delegate, and enable App Mode only when the headset doesn't persist it. (Split from the original combined client task.)

## Requirements
- [ ] On connect: subscribe to the button-event characteristic (UUID from the A1 capture)
- [ ] Write `appModeEnablePayload` only if App Mode is not persistent (per the persistence experiment)
- [ ] In `bleDidUpdateButtonValue`: parse via `BlueParrottEventParser`, dispatch to `BlueParrottButtonDelegate` on the main queue; log unknown payloads (never misclassify)

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's happy-path example.
- Files to modify: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift` (event extension)
- Dependencies: BLE core/lifecycle task, A1 capture (characteristic UUID + enable payload), persistence experiment, BlueParrottEventParser

## Verification

- [ ] Runs under `make test-mac`

## Acceptance Criteria
Contributes to epic #1, #2, #5.

title: Build A2 GATT explorer and run the App-Mode persistence experiment
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase A2 + Key experiment)

## Context
Determine whether App/SDK mode is persisted on the headset hardware. The result decides whether the Phase B client must replay the App-Mode enable handshake or can simply connect + subscribe.

## Requirements
- [ ] DEBUG `CBCentralManager` explorer: scan service 95665a00-…, enumerate services/characteristics + properties, subscribe to all notifiers, log notification hex
- [ ] Make the explorer runnable on macOS (requires the Bluetooth entitlement)
- [ ] Enable App Mode once via the iOS SDK, power-cycle/reconnect, then observe from macOS whether button notifications still flow with no re-handshake
- [ ] Record the decision (persistent / not persistent) on this issue and in the design doc

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's Phase A2 description. Note the explorer must be cross-platform (the doc's Files table places A2 in the iOS-only BPSniffer; it must also run on macOS for this experiment).
- Dependencies: macOS Bluetooth entitlement task

## Verification
- [ ] Manual (hardware): documented observation of persistent vs not persistent

## Acceptance Criteria
Informs the #1/#2 implementation path; gates the Phase B client (whether `writeAppModeEnable` is needed).

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: the A1 collector and the parser (after the entitlement lands).
close_reason: A2 GATT explorer built+tested (20 tests, iOS+macOS green), run on hardware. Decision: App Mode PERSISTS. Full protocol captured: button char 66339E60, opcodes 00=up/01=down/02=tap/03=double/04=long-press; recorded in design doc + issue.

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
A2 GATT explorer built, made runnable on macOS, and unit-tested.

Done (automatable):
- New BPGattExplorer.swift (#if DEBUG, cross-platform): standalone CBCentralManager client that scans service 95665a00-…, enumerates services/characteristics + properties, subscribes to every notifier, and logs notification hex via LogManager category "BPExplore". Prefers retrieveConnectedPeripherals (headset bonded for HFP may not advertise) then falls back to scanning. Handles all CBManagerState cases incl. .unauthorized.
- Runnable on macOS: file is compiled into the VoiceCodeMac target (not excluded), launched in DEBUG macOS builds from HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.activate()/deactivate(); the com.apple.security.device.bluetooth entitlement (b4i.2) is present.
- 20 unit tests (BPGattExplorerTests.swift, #if DEBUG, cross-platform): hex/property-description/subscribable/log-line formatting + construction/teardown safety. Pass under both `make test` (iOS) and `make test-mac` (macOS). Full macOS unit suite green (1572 tests, 0 failures); iOS suite green. (The only red was a pre-existing VoiceCodeMacUITests biometric/system-auth env failure, unrelated.)

Pending (manual, hardware required — cannot be done by an automated agent):
- The App-Mode persistence experiment itself: enable App Mode once on iOS, power-cycle the headset, observe from macOS whether button NOTIFY lines flow with no re-handshake. Step-by-step procedure documented in docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md §3 "Key experiment".

DECISION: PENDING — not yet observed. The result (persistent / not persistent) must be recorded here and in the design doc once run on hardware; it sets BlueParrottBLEManager.appModePersistent for Phase B (b4i.10).

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
Independent re-verification (fresh agent, did not trust prior claim): macOS unit suite green — 675 tests, 0 failures, all 20 BPGattExplorerTests passed; iOS 'make build' = TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED (explorer compiles cross-platform). Only red is VoiceCodeMacUITests-Runner timing out enabling automation mode (pre-existing UI-test env issue, unrelated).

Automatable harness is COMPLETE: BPGattExplorer.swift (#if DEBUG, cross-platform), compiled into VoiceCodeMac (not excluded), launched DEBUG-only from HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.activate()/deactivate(), entitlement from b4i.2. BPGattExplorerTests not excluded from either target (runs under make test + make test-mac). Design doc section 3 has the step-by-step experiment procedure + Decision: PENDING.

REMAINING (cannot be done by an automated agent): the App-Mode persistence experiment itself — enable App Mode once on iOS, power-cycle the headset, observe from macOS whether button NOTIFY lines flow with no re-handshake — requires a physical BlueParrott headset and human observation. Persistent/not-persistent decision stays PENDING until run on hardware; it sets BlueParrottBLEManager.appModePersistent and gates Phase B (b4i.10). Marking blocked on the manual hardware step.

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
Independent re-verification (fresh agent, did not trust prior comments — re-ran tests from a clean read of the working tree).

Automatable harness CONFIRMED complete and green:
- BPGattExplorer.swift (untracked, #if DEBUG, cross-platform): standalone CBCentralManager client — scans service 95665a00-…, prefers retrieveConnectedPeripherals then falls back to scanForPeripherals (headset is HFP-bonded and may not advertise — design Risk #3), enumerates services/characteristics with GATT properties, subscribes to every notify/indicate characteristic, logs notification hex via LogManager category 'BPExplore'. Handles all CBManagerState cases incl. .unauthorized/.unsupported/@unknown.
- Runnable on macOS: wired into HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.activate()/deactivate() under #if DEBUG && os(macOS) (startGattExplorer/stopGattExplorer, idempotent); com.apple.security.device.bluetooth entitlement present from b4i.2.
- Tests: BPGattExplorerTests.swift (untracked, #if DEBUG, cross-platform, not excluded in project.yml). Ran THIS session: make test-mac-class CLASS=BPGattExplorerTests -> 19 passed / 0 failures (VoiceCodeMacTests); make test-class CLASS=BPGattExplorerTests -> 19 passed / 0 failures (VoiceCodeTests). TEST SUCCEEDED on both schemes. (Prior comment said 20; the file actually has 19 — minor count discrepancy, all green.)

DECISION: still PENDING. Requirements #3 (enable App Mode once on iOS, power-cycle, observe from macOS whether button NOTIFY lines flow with no re-handshake) and #4 (record persistent/not-persistent here + in design doc) require a physical BlueParrott headset and human observation — impossible for an automated agent (no CoreBluetooth/hardware in CI). Design doc section 3 'Experiment procedure' + 'Decision: PENDING' are in place. Blocked on the manual hardware step; result sets BlueParrottBLEManager.appModePersistent and gates Phase B (b4i.10).

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
DECISION: App Mode PERSISTS (observed 2026-06-02 on firmware 2.6.4).

Evidence (macOS BPExplore log, logs-20260602-212235.txt): the Mac connected fresh and the A2 explorer only subscribed/read — NO enable write — yet the headset reported mode "sdk" (D24B6EC0 → 73 64 6b) and owner "Untethered" (C3356EE0 → ASCII), and streamed button events on press. App Mode survived the phone→Mac handoff with no re-handshake.

=> Phase B (b4i.9/b4i.10): set appModePersistent = true; connect + subscribe + parse, no writeAppModeEnable in the normal path. Keep the conditional enable only as a fallback for a never-enabled/factory-reset headset (write "sdk" to D24B6EC0).

CAPTURED PROTOCOL (frozen for b4i.4 parser):
- Button-event characteristic: 66339E60-D55A-11E5-B7CB-0002A5D5C51B [read|notify]
- Opcodes: 0x01=down, 0x00=up, 0x02=tap, 0x03=double-tap. long-press NOT captured (needs a held-button press). NOTE: this differs from the doc's old placeholder (up is 0x00, not 0x02) — placeholders now corrected in the design doc.
- mode char D24B6EC0 = "sdk"; appName char C3356EE0 = "Untethered"; firmware F3F8A600 = "2.6.4".

FOLLOW-UPS:
- A single tap emits THREE notifications (down,up,tap); double emits five. b4i.10 dispatcher must not double-drive the state machine (iOS SDK evidently de-dupes).
- Explorer logged setNotifyValue "attribute could not be found" for all notify chars (issued as a burst) yet 66339E60 still notified. b4i.9 should subscribe to just the button char, verify isNotifying, discover the CCCD if it recurs.
- Need a held-press capture to get the long-press opcode.

Design doc updated (§3 Key experiment: PERSISTENT + capture-results table; BPGatt constants + parser opcodes + test example replaced with captured values).

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
LONG-PRESS CAPTURED (logs-20260602-212903.txt, firmware 2.6.4). Complete gesture opcode map for char 66339E60 is now frozen:
- 0x00 = up
- 0x01 = down
- 0x02 = tap
- 0x03 = double-tap
- 0x04 = long-press (fires ~1s after down)

Observed twice: a hold emits 01 (down) → 04 (long-press, ~1s later) → 00 (up on release); fires once at the threshold, no tap/double on release.

Phase B dispatch note: down/up bracket EVERY gesture (tap=01,00,02; double=01,00,01,00,03; hold=01,04,00). b4i.10 must drive PTT off either down/up OR the gesture codes, not both (else a PTT hold also fires long-press→interrupt mid-recording).

Design doc updated: capture table, parser switch (added case 0x04 → .longPress), and parser test example now include long-press. The b4i.4 parser is fully specified.

title: Implement BlueParrottEventParser (pure byte→event) with unit tests
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (byte parser) + #4-verification-strategy

## Context
Pure decode of a notification payload to a logical gesture — the unit-testable core of the macOS client. Opcode constants come from the A1 capture.

## Requirements
- [ ] `BlueParrottButtonEvent` enum (down/up/tap/doubleTap/longPress)
- [ ] `BlueParrottEventParser.parse(Data) -> BlueParrottButtonEvent?`, returning nil for empty/unknown payloads
- [ ] Populate the opcode table from the captured bytes (A1)

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's parser example.
- New files: parser in `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift` (or a small dedicated file)
- Dependencies: A1 collector (captured byte format)

## Verification
- [ ] Unit tests: each gesture decodes to the right event; empty payload → nil; unknown opcode → nil — using the captured real-device byte sequences

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #3.

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: the A2 / persistence experiment (after the A1 capture).
close_reason: BlueParrottEventParser + BlueParrottButtonEvent in a dedicated cross-platform file. Opcodes frozen from A2 capture: 00=up,01=down,02=tap,03=double,04=long. 8 unit tests incl. real captured tap/double/long sequences + empty/unknown→nil; green on make test (iOS) and make test-mac (macOS).

title: Implement BlueParrottBLEManager macOS CoreBluetooth client with tests
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase B + API Design) + #4-verification-strategy

## Context
The macOS CoreBluetooth client that connects, optionally enables App Mode, subscribes to button events, parses them, and emits `BlueParrottButtonDelegate` — the replacement event source for the mute proxy.

## Requirements
- [ ] `BLECentral` / `BLECentralEvents` test seam + a real `CBCentralManager`-backed adapter that delivers callbacks on the main queue
- [ ] Connect/retry/re-arm state machine mirroring the iOS manager (fast retries → infinite 30s slow retry; `maxRetries = 5`; DEBUG `testInSlowRetry` hook)
- [ ] On connect: subscribe to the button-event characteristic; write `appModeEnablePayload` only if App Mode is not persistent (per the experiment)
- [ ] Parse notifications via `BlueParrottEventParser`; dispatch to `BlueParrottButtonDelegate` on the main queue
- [ ] Handle `CBManagerState` (poweredOff/resetting/unauthorized/unsupported)

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's API Design + happy/error-path examples; use the characteristic UUIDs and handshake payload from A1.
- New files: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift`
- Dependencies: A1 collector, macOS entitlement, persistence experiment, BlueParrottEventParser

## Verification
- [ ] Unit tests with `FakeBLECentral` + `DelegateSpy`: transient failure → slow-retry fallback; button-down → delegate call
- [ ] Test file is `#if os(macOS)` and added to the iOS `VoiceCodeTests` `excludes`; runs under `make test-mac`

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #4 (retry/state-machine tests); contributes to #1/#2/#5.
delete_reason: Split into voice-code-macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth-b4i.9 (core/lifecycle) and voice-code-macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth-b4i.10 (subscribe/parse/dispatch) — original task too large for one session

title: Implement BlueParrottBLEManager core: CoreBluetooth seam, adapter, connect/retry state machine
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase B + API Design)

## Context
The macOS client's foundation — the CoreBluetooth abstraction plus the connect/retry/re-arm lifecycle — split from event handling so it is a single focused unit. Mirrors the iOS manager's structure. (Split from the original combined client task.)

## Requirements
- [ ] `BlueParrottBLEManager` (macOS) skeleton: `@Published` connection state, `BlueParrottButtonDelegate` hookup point
- [ ] `BLECentral` / `BLECentralEvents` test seam + a real `CBCentralManager`-backed adapter that delivers callbacks on the main queue and wires `centralDelegate = self`
- [ ] Scan for service 95665a00-…, connect, discover services
- [ ] Connect/retry/re-arm state machine mirroring iOS (fast retries → infinite 30s slow retry; `maxRetries = 5`; DEBUG `testInSlowRetry` hook)
- [ ] Handle `CBManagerState` (poweredOff/resetting/unauthorized/unsupported)

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's API Design + error-path example. The service UUID is known from the header; characteristic-level subscribe/parse is the sibling task.
- New files: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift` (skeleton + lifecycle)
- Dependencies: macOS Bluetooth entitlement

## Verification
- [ ] Unit tests with `FakeBLECentral`: transient connect failure → slow-retry fallback; `CBManagerState` handling
- [ ] Test file is `#if os(macOS)` and added to the iOS `VoiceCodeTests` `excludes`; runs under `make test-mac`

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #4 (connect/retry/re-arm tests with a faked BLECentral).

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: A1 collector, A2/persistence experiment, and the parser (after the entitlement lands).
close_reason: BlueParrottBLEManager foundation: BLECentral/BLECentralEvents seam, real CBCentralManager adapter (main-queue callbacks, retrieveConnected→scan→connect→discover-services), connect/retry/re-arm state machine (fast retries → infinite slow retry), full CBManagerState handling. BlueParrottButtonDelegate extracted to a shared cross-platform file. 18 unit tests via injected fake; green on make test-mac. Subscribe/parse/dispatch + conditional App-Mode enable deferred to b4i.10.

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
Implemented the macOS BLE manager core (no hardware needed; all unit-tested).

New files:
- BlueParrottBLEManager.swift (#if os(macOS)): BLECentral/BLECentralEvents seam + a real CBCentralManager-backed CBCentralAdapter (queue: nil → callbacks on main; wires centralDelegate=self). scanForButtonService prefers retrieveConnectedPeripherals(95665a00-…) then scanForPeripherals (HFP-bonded headset may not advertise — Risk #3), connects, discovers services (characteristic-level subscribe deferred to b4i.10). Connect/retry/re-arm state machine mirrors iOS BlueParrottButtonManager: initialDelay 1s, retryDelay 2s, maxRetries=5, then infinite slowRetryDelay 30s; reconnect()/disconnect re-arm fast retry; start() idempotent and waits for .poweredOn. handleManagerState covers poweredOff/resetting/unauthorized/unsupported/unknown. DEBUG testInSlowRetry/testRetryCount hooks. delegate/appModePersistent/isSDKModeEnabled are hookup points b4i.4/b4i.10 consume.
- BlueParrottButtonDelegate.swift (platform-agnostic): EXTRACTED the BlueParrottButtonDelegate protocol out of the iOS-only (and macOS-excluded) BlueParrottButtonManager.swift into a shared file compiled into both targets, so the macOS manager can declare the delegate hookup. Design calls it 'platform-agnostic — reused verbatim'. iOS unaffected (same module).
- BlueParrottBLEManagerTests.swift (#if os(macOS)): 18 tests via FakeBLECentral + synchronous ScheduleRecorder — initial-connect scheduling, fast→slow retry exhaustion (maxRetries+1), slow-retry-then-connect reset, non-retryable no-reschedule, connect/disconnect/reconnect re-arm, stop halts+cancels, and CBManagerState (poweredOff/resetting/unauthorized/unsupported). Added to iOS VoiceCodeTests excludes in project.yml (mirrors BluetoothAudioMonitorTests); runs under make test-mac.

Tests run THIS session:
- make test-mac → VoiceCodeMacTests 1299 tests, 0 failures (incl. the 18 new). (Only red = pre-existing VoiceCodeMacUITests automation-mode timeout, environmental/unrelated.)
- make test → iOS full unit suite TEST SUCCEEDED, 0 failures (confirms the protocol extraction causes no iOS regression).

Purely additive: nothing instantiates BlueParrottBLEManager yet — HeadsetRemoteCommandManager rewiring is b4i.6, event subscribe/parse/dispatch is b4i.10. Not committed (code review next).
